passages.text: Therefore let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God, instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
passages.sermon:
We must leave the basic teachings about Christ.
We must move forward to maturity.
We should not lay the foundation again.
This foundation includes repentance from dead works.
It includes faith in God.
It includes teaching about baptisms.
It includes the laying on of hands.
It includes the resurrection of the dead.
It includes eternal judgment.
passages.original: Διὸ ἀφέντες τὸν τῆς ἀρχῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ λόγον ἐπὶ τὴν τελειότητα φερώμεθα μὴ πάλιν θεμέλιον καταβαλλόμενοι μετανοίας ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων καὶ πίστεως ἐπὶ Θεόν βαπτισμῶν διδαχὴν ἐπιθέσεώς τε χειρῶν ἀναστάσεώς τε νεκρῶν καὶ κρίματος αἰωνίου

passages.text: And this we will do, if God permits.
passages.sermon:
We will do this.
We will go on to maturity.
We will leave the elementary teachings about Christ.
We will do it if God permits.
God must allow us to do this.
passages.original: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσομεν ἐάνπερ ἐπιτρέπῃ ὁ Θεός

passages.text: It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit, who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age— and then have fallen away—to be restored to repentance, because they themselves are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.
passages.sermon:
Some people have once been enlightened.
They have tasted the heavenly gift.
They have shared in the Holy Spirit.
They have tasted the goodness of the word of God.
They have tasted the powers of the coming age.
These people have then fallen away.
It is impossible to restore them again to repentance.
They are crucifying the Son of God again for themselves.
They are exposing Him to public shame.
passages.original: Ἀδύνατον γὰρ τοὺς ἅπαξ φωτισθέντας γευσαμένους τε τῆς δωρεᾶς τῆς ἐπουρανίου καὶ μετόχους γενηθέντας Πνεύματος Ἁγίου καὶ καλὸν γευσαμένους Θεοῦ ῥῆμα δυνάμεις τε μέλλοντος αἰῶνος καὶ παραπεσόντας πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν εἰς μετάνοιαν ἀνασταυροῦντας ἑαυτοῖς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ παραδειγματίζοντας

passages.text: For land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended receives the blessing of God.
passages.sermon:
The land receives rain often.
The rain falls on the land.
The land drinks in the rain.
The land produces a crop.
The crop is useful.
The crop is for the people who work the land.
God blesses the land that produces a useful crop.
passages.original: Γῆ γὰρ ἡ πιοῦσα τὸν ἐπ’ αὐτῆς ἐρχόμενον πολλάκις ὑετόν καὶ τίκτουσα βοτάνην εὔθετον ἐκείνοις δι’ οὓς καὶ γεωργεῖται μεταλαμβάνει εὐλογίας ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. In the end it will be burned.
passages.sermon:
Land can produce thorns and thistles.
This land is worthless.
A curse is near for this land.
In the end, people will burn this land.
passages.original: ἐκφέρουσα δὲ ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους ἀδόκιμος καὶ κατάρας ἐγγύς ἧς τὸ τέλος εἰς καῦσιν

passages.text: Even though we speak like this, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case—things that accompany salvation.
passages.sermon:
I speak to you, beloved people.
I have said hard things.
But I am convinced of better things for you.
These better things belong to salvation.
I believe you have what comes with salvation.
passages.original: Πεπείσμεθα δὲ περὶ ὑμῶν ἀγαπητοί τὰ κρείσσονα καὶ ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας εἰ καὶ οὕτως λαλοῦμεν

passages.text: For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.
passages.sermon:
God is not unjust.
God does not forget your work.
God remembers the love you have shown for His name.
You have served the saints.
You continue to serve the saints.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἄδικος ὁ Θεὸς ἐπιλαθέσθαι τοῦ ἔργου ὑμῶν καὶ τῆς ἀγάπης ἧς ἐνεδείξασθε εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ διακονήσαντες τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ διακονοῦντες

passages.text: We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.
passages.sermon:
We speak to you, beloved believers in Christ.
We want each of you to show diligence.
Show the same diligence you have shown before.
Continue this diligence until the very end.
This will make your hope certain.
passages.original: Ἐπιθυμοῦμεν δὲ ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι σπουδὴν πρὸς τὴν πληροφορίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἄχρι τέλους

passages.text: Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised.
passages.sermon:
You must not become lazy.
You must imitate certain people.
These people receive what God promised.
They receive it through faith.
They also receive it through patience.
passages.original: ἵνα μὴ νωθροὶ γένησθε μιμηταὶ δὲ τῶν διὰ πίστεως καὶ μακροθυμίας κληρονομούντων τὰς ἐπαγγελίας

passages.text: When God made His promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself, saying, “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants.”
passages.sermon:
God made a promise to Abraham.
God is the highest authority.
No one is greater than God.
God could not swear by anyone greater than Himself.
God swore by Himself.
God said, “I will surely bless you.”
God also said, “I will multiply your descendants.”
passages.original: Τῷ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐπαγγειλάμενος ὁ Θεός ἐπεὶ κατ’ οὐδενὸς εἶχεν μείζονος ὀμόσαι ὤμοσεν καθ’ ἑαυτοῦ λέγων Εἰ μὴν εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω σε καὶ πληθύνων πληθυνῶ σε

passages.text: And so Abraham, after waiting patiently, obtained the promise.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man of faith.
\r\nAbraham waited patiently.
\r\nGod had made a promise to Abraham.
\r\nAbraham received the promise from God.
\r\nAbraham obtained what God had promised him.
passages.original: καὶ οὕτως μακροθυμήσας ἐπέτυχεν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας

passages.text: Men swear by someone greater than themselves, and their oath serves as a confirmation to end all argument.
passages.sermon:
People make oaths.
They swear by someone greater than themselves.
Their oath confirms what they say.
The oath ends every argument.
passages.original: Ἄνθρωποι γὰρ κατὰ τοῦ μείζονος ὀμνύουσιν καὶ πάσης αὐτοῖς ἀντιλογίας πέρας εἰς βεβαίωσιν ὁ ὅρκος

passages.text: So when God wanted to make the unchanging nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise, He guaranteed it with an oath.
passages.sermon:
God wanted to show His purpose clearly.
God’s purpose does not change.
God wanted the heirs of the promise to know this.
God made a guarantee.
God gave an oath.
God used the oath to show His unchanging purpose to the heirs of the promise.
passages.original: ἐν ᾧ περισσότερον βουλόμενος ὁ Θεὸς ἐπιδεῖξαι τοῖς κληρονόμοις τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τὸ ἀμετάθετον τῆς βουλῆς αὐτοῦ ἐμεσίτευσεν ὅρκῳ

passages.text: Thus by two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged.
passages.sermon:
God cannot lie.
God made two unchangeable things.
These two things give us certainty.
We have run to God for safety.
We want to take hold of the hope God gives us.
These two unchangeable things give us strong encouragement.
passages.original: ἵνα διὰ δύο πραγμάτων ἀμεταθέτων ἐν οἷς ἀδύνατον ψεύσασθαι τὸν Θεόν ἰσχυρὰν παράκλησιν ἔχωμεν οἱ καταφυγόντες κρατῆσαι τῆς προκειμένης ἐλπίδος

passages.text: We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain, where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf. He has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
passages.sermon:
God gave us a promise.
This promise gives us hope.
This hope is strong and sure.
This hope is like an anchor for our souls.
This hope keeps us safe and steady.
This hope goes into the inner sanctuary behind the curtain.
The inner sanctuary is the most holy place with God.
Jesus went into this most holy place for us.
Jesus is our forerunner.
Jesus became a high priest forever.
Jesus is a high priest in the order of Melchizedek.
passages.original: ἣν ὡς ἄγκυραν ἔχομεν τῆς ψυχῆς ἀσφαλῆ τε καὶ βεβαίαν καὶ εἰσερχομένην εἰς τὸ ἐσώτερον τοῦ καταπετάσματος ὅπου πρόδρομος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἀρχιερεὺς γενόμενος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα
